To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) a new object detection and tracking algorithm is presented, b) it can be used to adaptively sample the video frame and c) it is shown that the computational complexity of this system is reduced by 50%.

we have designed and implemented a system that can adapt its sampling rate and computational complexity to the scene, resulting in an average reduction in computation by 50% for the same accuracy as a fixed sampling rate system.

we propose a low-complexity object detection and tracking system design that scales the computational complexity of object detection with the salience of each captured frame, resulting in significant reduction of the computational complexity of a high resolution video object tracking system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a low complexity, adaptive, content aware video processing system.
developing a real time object tracking system that is able to scale its computational complexity with the amount of salience in the scene.
the problem of real time object detection and tracking for high resolution video.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed system design reduces the complexity of object detection for tracking in high resolution video by 50% while maintaining real time operation.
a novel control system is presented that adaptively adjusts the sampling density for each frame based on the amount of foreground activity.
the proposed adaptive compressed sensing system can adaptively adjust the system throughput to meet the requirements of a given scene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new adaptive sampling and control system to perform object detection for object tracking in high resolution videos on embedded systems.
we are developing a system that can adapt to the amount of activity in the scene and can scale down to a minimum level of complexity.
we have developed a system that can detect objects in real-time and can adapt to changes in scene activity, while reducing the overall computational load.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed adaptive sampling method can be used to reduce the computational complexity of object detection algorithms by a factor of 50% while maintaining the same accuracy.
the proposed system design can be applied to any object detection system that can be implemented in real time.
by using a compressed sensing approach, we can achieve a reduction in computational complexity of 50% on average, and 70% in the worst-case scenario.
